# product-lifecycle — Skill Analysis

## What the skill does

Queries the Red Hat Product Life Cycle (PLC) API for support phases, EOL
dates, and OCP version compatibility of Red Hat products and OLM operators,
and resolves operator upgrade paths (which versions, catalog sources, and
channels reach a target OCP version). Leaf skill — no sub-skills;
`cluster-update-advisor` is a consumer, not a dependency.

## Inputs and invocation

- Two CLI subcommands via `python3 product-lifecycle/scripts/plc_lookup.py`:
  - `products <name> [--ocp X.Y] [--productsfile F]` — substring product
    lookup, per-version status/phases, ocp_compatible when --ocp given.
  - `olm-check --ocp X.Y (--olmv0 '<json>' | --olmv1 '<json>')
    [--compatibleonly] [--productsfile F] [--packagemanifestsfile F]` —
    batch operator check; `--compatibleonly` restricts to compatible
    versions and emits reachable-upgrade output (source_catalogs filtered
    to SemVer-higher compatible versions). `--olmv0` also reads cluster
    packagemanifests (mocked via --packagemanifestsfile).
- Each eval case is one natural-language query naming operators, versions,
  management type (OLMv0 Subscription vs OLMv1 ClusterExtension), target
  OCP version, and what to report; `response_schema` constrains the JSON
  answer shape. One query per invocation → case mode (the script's
  array-of-operators support is within a single request, not multi-case).

## Outputs

stdout-only — the script prints JSON to stdout; the agent writes no files.
The scored artifact is the agent's conversational JSON answer: aggregate
counts, compatibility booleans, normalized lifecycle status enum
(supported|maintenance|extended|end-of-maintenance|eol|unknown), and
upgrade-path specifics (upgrade_catalog, upgrade_versions_available,
compatible_versions).

## Good vs bad output

Good: correct invocation shape with mock-file flags; exact ground-truth
fields (e.g. plc_olmv0_batch_check: checked=3, found=2 — grafana-operator
correctly counted as not-found, not incompatible); statuses normalized to
the enum ("End of life" → "eol"). Bad: lifecycle data asserted without
invoking the script; raw API statuses instead of the enum; not-found
packages reported as incompatible; downgrade versions listed as upgrade
paths; OLMv0-only source_catalogs expected on OLMv1 results.

## Edge cases

Three-valued ocp_compatible (true/false/null); error entries with
available_versions (package found, version untracked) vs plain not-found;
version normalization (v5.9.14 → 5.9); duplicate PLC products (script
prefers entries with openshift_compatibility); packagemanifest_error
degraded-but-complete output.

## External services / interception

The script calls https://access.redhat.com/product-life-cycles/api/v2/products
(urllib) and, for --olmv0, `oc get packagemanifests` against a cluster.
Both are [EXTERNAL: System] and blocked via `inputs.tools`; frozen mocks
are provisioned into every case workspace via `dataset.workspace.files`
(mock_products.json — PLC API snapshot captured 2026-11-05, trimmed to 9
products; mock_packagemanifests.json — hand-crafted `oc get packagemanifests
-A -o json`). No AskUserQuestion, no MCP tools.

## Dataset

Converted from `evals/skills/product-lifecycle/test_cases.yaml` (9 cases).
The upstream `system_prompt.md` rules (OLMv0/OLMV1 split, --compatibleonly,
mock-file flags, don't guess) are ported into `runner.system_prompt`.
